answers.question: Is context.db created at MCP initialize, at first tool call, or at install time?
answers.answer: At first tool call, not at initialize or install. ADR-0007 makes the server stateless (no per-connection work at initialize; it only returns instructions/DiscoverResult). Install is a bare git checkout with no setup step. The db file is created lazily when a tool handler first opens it.
answers.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md:4 'Stateless server: no per-connection state'; docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md GP1 row 'project read after initialize' (project path resolution, not db open); docs/v2/adr/0002-single-context-db.md (db path and engine rules, no open-timing statement).

answers.question: What are the 7 tool names and 7 schemas exactly, since §1 GS5 says 'tools/list (7 tools)' but §10 Q12 lists 9 ctx_ names?
answers.answer: 9 tools is current: ctx_execute, ctx_batch, ctx_index, ctx_search, ctx_resume, ctx_stats, ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade, ctx_purge. PRD-v2.md §16 (dated 2026-10-14, the latest round) states this line 'replaces G4 doctor/upgrade removed' and supersedes the earlier §7 list of 7. ADR-0010 (Accepted 2026-10-14) confirms ctx_doctor and ctx_upgrade are kept as tools, rebuilt for v2. ADR-0007 §5 also says tools/list returns 'the 9 tools in a fixed order'. TECH-SPEC §1 GS5 and GP1 ('7 tools') are stale and were not updated after PRD §16 / ADR-0010.
answers.evidence: PRD-v2.md:289 'Tools (replaces G4 ...): 9 tools'; docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md Decision; docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md:5 'tools/list returns the 9 tools in a fixed order'; docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:38,287 say '7 tools'.

answers.question: For GS9 (stateless server/discover vs initialize at two MCP versions), is this one code path with a version switch, or two server builds?
answers.answer: One code path, one build. ADR-0007 is explicit: one server, one SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/server v2.x) handles both the 2026-07-28 server/discover RPC and the 2025-xx initialize handshake through the SDK's own protocol-version negotiation. This is stated as 'not a fallback in our code: one server and one tool set, answered in the version the client asks for.'
answers.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md Decision §2: 'through the same SDK's version negotiation... one server and one tool set'; GS9 (TECH-SPEC.md:40) 'passes GP1/GP2 as a stateless server and as an initialize server, with identical bytes'.

answers.question: Does 'no fallback chains' (owner decision) forbid try/catch retry logic entirely, or only forbid silently falling back to a different data source on error?
answers.answer: It forbids silently switching between alternate code paths or data sources (one path per behaviour), not try/catch error handling as such. README §22 states the rule as 'one path per behaviour.' Every place the rule is applied in the ADRs shows the same scope: ADR-0002 bans a retry *loop* on busy errors (not error handling, a looping alternate path); ADR-0010 bans *trying several install-mode strategies* and instead picks the one path from data (adapter table); ADR-0001 names the v1 failure mode this prevents: per-adapter runtime fallbacks that made a bug untraceable to one code path. A try/catch that reports one error and stops is fine; a try/catch that then attempts a second strategy is the banned pattern.
answers.evidence: docs/v2/README.md:22 'No fallback chains: one path per behaviour'; docs/v2/adr/0002-single-context-db.md Decision §2 'No retry loop'; docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md 'ctx_upgrade: one path per install mode, no fallback'; docs/v2/adr/0001-claude-code-reference-contract.md:8 'v1 handled these differences inside each adapter with runtime fallbacks, so a bug could not be traced to a single code path.'

archaeology.introduced_by: v1 src/db-base.ts withRetry (commit 09185d3e refactor: extract withRetry as standalone export) and its busy-loop fix history (7afa0f45, 065799f8, f6c61535)
archaeology.original_intent: v1 added retry/EXCLUSIVE-locking fallback branches to survive SQLITE_BUSY under concurrent writers, per commit messages on #560/#642
archaeology.regression_risk: If v2 reintroduces any retry loop or alternate-path fallback in the db layer, it repeats v1's #985 CPU-spin bug (named directly in ADR-0002's Context section as traced to src/db-base.ts:446's withRetry busy loop)
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: db writes must rely only on node:sqlite {timeout:5000} + BEGIN IMMEDIATE (ADR-0002 §2); no retry loop, no second code path on SQLITE_BUSY

answers.question: Since skills are removed from the repo (Q4/Q4b) but /ctx-stats, /ctx-doctor, /ctx-upgrade are shipped as skills (Q3), where do these three skill files live if not under .claude/skills/context-mode-ops?
answers.answer: Not a real contradiction: two different things share the word 'skill'. Q4/Q4b and TECH-SPEC §3.10 remove v1's per-agent copies and the v1 removed-agent paths (e.g. the old .claude/skills/context-mode-ops/ tree listed for deletion). The v2 user-command skills live in one new source dir at repo root, 'skills/' (3 files: one SKILL.md each for ctx-stats, ctx-doctor, ctx-upgrade), each with disable-model-invocation:true, and host manifests point at that single dir — no per-agent copies.
answers.evidence: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md §3.9 (line ~207): 'One source dir skills/ (3 files). Manifests point at it; no per-agent copies'; docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:241 lists the removed v1 path '.claude/skills/context-mode-ops/' among deleted v1-only trees, which is a different, old path.

docGapFinding.section: §3.9 vs §3.10/line 241 — the new skills/ dir and the removed v1 .claude/skills path are never cross-referenced, which reads as a conflict on first pass
